notes: Councillor Roach opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Waterloo Park Plan Update – Project Launch
notes: Report No.: COM2025-023
Prepared By: Anna lee Sangster

Anna lee Sangster gave a presentation with the brief history of Waterloo Park and the Park Plan, as well as highlighting the launch of the Update to the Waterloo Park Plan including the future community engagement, and the timeline of the upcoming plan.

Gordon Greavette, Chair, Waterloo Park Advisory Committee gave a presentation thanking the committee for their accomplishments over the life of the committee, thanking the staff for their advice and the enhancements made to the park, and thanking the many past volunteers for their assistance in implementing the many objectives of the plan.
Hannah Gardiner, Resident of Waterloo gave a presentation sharing their experiences of coordinating events in the Park, and highlighted the importance of small scale events.
Hannah Gardiner also offered solutions to the issues they have faced in planning events. Hannah Gardiner responded to questions of Council.

notes: Informal Public Meeting

items.title: Zoning By-Law Amendment Z-25-23
notes: VanMar Developments
171 King GP Corp
167-171 King Street South
Prepared by: Wendy Fisher and Kaitlyn Bisch
Ward No.: Ward 7 – Uptown Ward

Kaitlyn Bisch gave a presentation outlining the proposed development, including the site context, background information on Official Plan Amendment 58, proposed site plans and renderings, and the requested zoning by-law amendments. She then responded to questions of Council.

Paul Leveck, Representative, VanMar Developments 171 King GP Corp spoke about the developer’s perspective on the project, including the appreciation of the scale of the project and the people that it’ll bring to the core, as well as the importance of the heritage building on the site. Andrea Sinclair, Partner, MHBC Planning continued the presentation further detailing the development, including the site statistics, the heritage considerations, and the potential amenities for the building. Andrea Sinclair responded to questions of Council. Kaitlyn Bisch also responded to questions of Council. Paul Leveck also responded to questions of Council. Vanessa Hicks, Associate, MHBC Planning also responded to questions of Council.

Bob Publicover, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the changes coming to Uptown, the potential timing of the development, and whether there is a need for two towers on the site. Kaitlyn Bisch responded to questions of Council.

Geoff Bell, Resident of Waterloo spoke about living in the Uptown core, the height of the development, the need for housing that supports the needs of the community, and concerns with wind speeds and noise surrounding the development.
Igor Rayt, Resident of Waterloo spoke about concerns living in the neighbourhood, specifically surrounding privacy, sunlight, and wind. Wendy Fisher responded to questions of Council.
Brenda Dunbar, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the size of the building compared to the neighbourhood, as well as the wind issues and the lack of landscaping at ground level.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Wright spoke about impacts of Bill 5 and the potential impact on endangered species by invasive species and the impacts of climate change. Councillor Wright asked if the City has a comprehensive plan and tracking system for invasive species. Staff will provide an update to Council.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Vasic wanted to highlight two Ward 5 businesses. She and the Mayor visited Mamma’s Pizza on Lexington Road by Davenport Road, which is their new location. It’s a woman-owned Toronto chain that has been running for more than 50 years. As well, Snugglers Furniture on Weber Street North at Bridgeport Road East celebrated their 50th anniversary. It was a great celebration of local entrepreneurship.

Councillor Wright offered her thanks to the City for helping with the street closure on King Street for the Mayor’s Oktoberfest Market on Sunday, October 5 in partnership with the Uptown BIA. It was a hot day, but so many people came out and had a great time.
Councillor Roe wanted to say kudos to staff for the amazing paving work they did in Thorndale Park. It’s fantastic and the neighbourhood loves it.
